summary: Console alert snooze & group mute reset after session refresh leading to duplicate notifications post-retention-compact
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that alerts they had previously snoozed or group-muted through the Console are being reset after their browser session refreshes or when retention compaction runs. Shortly after retention compaction (automatic housekeeping job) completes for older alert state records, the same alerts re-fire and notify on-call, creating duplicate notifications and confusion.

Impact: Multiple noisy page-outs for AcmeAnalytics production alerting routes. Customer says 5 duplicate pages within 30 minutes after compaction window. Business impact: on-call fatigue and potential missed triage for other incidents.

Environment: Production (us-east-1) Console, alerting subsystem (scheduled jobs + Redis state cache + retention compact job). Affects enterprise tenant on dedicated account.

Observed timeframe: First seen 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC after scheduled retention-compact job; customer reported repeat 2026-03-10 07:30 UTC after session refresh.

Expected behavior: Snooze and group mute actions persist across browser sessions and through retention/compact events until the configured snooze/mute expiration. Alerts that are snoozed should not trigger notifications until snooze expires.

Actual behavior: Snooze/mute entries appear to be invalidated after either (a) a console session refresh/login or (b) retention compaction of the alert-state table. The alert entries remain visible in UI but notification state behaves as active, causing notifications to be sent.

Additional notes: Customer used both individual alert snooze and group mute. They confirmed they were not manually unmuting. The Console shows last-snoozed-by and timestamp but notifications resumed as if no snooze existed.
steps_to_reproduce: Log into Console as an enterprise user with alerting permissions in us-east-1.
Navigate to Alerts -> Alert Rules and snooze a rule for 2 hours, confirm UI shows 'Snoozed until <timestamp>'.
Open a second browser tab and refresh the session (or sign out and sign back in).
Observe that UI still shows snooze, but wait for next alert evaluation cycle; customer observed notifications within next 5-10 minutes.
Trigger retention-compact job on a staging copy of the alert-state table (QA step) and observe whether notification state is preserved or reactivated.

2026-03-09T22:15:05Z INFO notifier: sending notification rule_id=rl-992 tenant=acmeanalytics channel=pagerduty
2026-03-10T07:29:21Z INFO session: user=a.patel re-authenticated; session_id=sess-4d33; cache-miss for alert_state shard=12
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: retention compaction is removing rows the notifier relies on and cache-refresh logic treats missing rows as active alerts.
Observed correlation between compaction window and customer-reported duplicate notifications for two separate tenants in us-east-1.
Cache layer (Redis) shows TTL for alert-state keys shorter than expected; TTLs appear to be reset after session refresh causing immediate cache miss and re-computation to active state.
Verified UI still renders 'snoozed' metadata from a denormalized column, but the live notifier reads from the compacted 'alert_state' table which may have had rows removed.
Related to schema migration performed 2026-02-28 that introduced denormalized last_snoozed column; suspected mismatch between authoritative table and denormalized UI source.
comments: Aisha Patel (support): Received initial report from customer 2026-03-10 08:05 UTC; escalated to SRE given P1 impact.

Diego Morales (SRE): I can reproduce on staging when running retention-compact against a copy of tenant data. Looks like notifier uses alert_state primary table; UI pulls from denormalized column in alerts config table. Need to reconcile authoritative source.
Samantha Lee (PM - Console): Adding label retention-compact and routing to console team; filing follow-up design review for authoritative state model.

Diego Morales (SRE): Temporary mitigation: increase Redis TTL for alert-state keys to 24h and pause compaction for affected shard 12 for AcmeAnalytics while we patch. Proceeding with change pending customer approval.
AcmeAnalytics (customer): Confirmed that after TTL bump they did not receive repeat pages for the 2-hour window. Requested ETA for permanent fix.
resolution: Workaround applied: Increased Redis TTL for alert-state keys for affected tenant and paused compaction on shard 12. Engineering to deploy a patch that ensures notifier reads authoritative snooze/mute state and UI reflects authoritative source. ETA for patch: 2026-03-15. Customer notified and will be kept in loop.
